reports.notes:
I rebuilt everything in my own code (recompute.py). Each group is reduced to exact counts: wins with ties counted as 1/2, and the number of tipped x untipped pairs. The pooled AUROC is total wins divided by total pairs. For the bootstrap I count how often each group is drawn and weight its wins and pairs by that count.

Results:
- Every point estimate in part_b and id_pairs_within (12 predictors x run-level, pairs, row-level) matches the JSON to 4 decimals.
- Replaying the script's RNG stream with my code reproduces all 48 CIs exactly, so the reported CIs are what the script's draws produce. The gaps from my own seeds are sampling noise.
- Own-seed gaps in Part B are at most 0.03 (largest: zs:global_full run upper bound, 0.0303). In the id pairs, the zs:pairwise row-level lower bound is off by up to 0.063 because the JSON value is an unlucky 2nd-percentile draw.
- The 29 Part B pairs are 10 night-night, 16 night-new and 3 new-new, as Nachtrag 2 states. The id pairs really do rest on one mixed base (K2-150), and their CI is degenerate.
- H1 ('not supported') holds under every seed I tried.
- The zs:global_full lower bound above 0.5 (0.5157) holds in only 66% of seeds, so it should not be quoted as excluding 0.5.

Descriptive extras, small samples, not tested:
- The pooled zs numbers lean on the night-night pairs (0.90/0.95 there vs 0.684 on the 19 pairs with a new run). gnn drops less (0.80 vs 0.737). struct goes the other way (0.60 vs 1.00) and wins all 16 night-new pairs whichever side is new, so its result is not a simple level shift between the two run batches.
- For gnn, untipped new runs score higher at the cut than untipped night runs in mixed groups (mean 0.165, n=5, vs 0.017, n=6). gnn wins 6/7 night-new pairs when the tipped run is new but only 6/9 when it is a night run (zs:global_full 6/7 vs 5/9).

reports.notes:
Method: my own code in partA_common.py and partA_recompute.py; analysis/vx_eval.py and vx_verdicts.py were read for definitions only, never imported. AUROC comes from explicit positive x negative comparisons, with ties counted as 0.5. For each block and predictor I build per-base win matrices W[b,b'] (positives of base b against negatives of base b'), plus one matrix per rounds-to-cut bin. A bootstrap draw with base multiplicities c then gives AUROC = c'Wc / ((c.npos)(c.nneg)) and time-matched AUROC = sum over bins of c'W_bin c / sum over bins of (c.npos_bin)(c.nneg_bin). This equals concatenating the drawn bases' rows, a base drawn twice counting twice, and equals a brute-force computation to 1e-12.

Verdict: every Part A number in vx_eval.json and vx_eval_refbag.json is what the pre-registered definitions produce: 1328 point values, all 464 CIs, and the H2 censoring block. No critical discrepancy. The listed minor items are Monte Carlo precision, not errors.

(1) The reported CIs carry Monte Carlo error of about 0.004-0.03 per endpoint at 2000 draws, so their third and fourth decimals are not meaningful. This is worst for topo tm (7 bases) and time tm.
(2) Ten CIs sit so close to 0 that whether they exclude it depends on the seed. Write-ups should not state 'excludes 0' or 'includes 0' for them without a caveat. Required predictors: glm zs:pairwise AUROC shift; time zs:pairwise tm shift-noise; time zs:global_full tm shift-noise. The H2 tm shift-noise lower bound (-0.0045 reported, -0.064 converged) is in the same situation.
(3) Noise has the same point value in time, glm and enf, because the id blocks are identical. Each arm still reports its own CI from its own draws; for gnn AUROC noise these are time [-0.2641, 0.1997], glm about [-0.266, 0.192] and enf [-0.2614, 0.1867]. This is by design (one set of draws per arm), but a write-up should cite one of them.
(4) H2 'GNN stable' depends on |shift| 0.0523 <= |noise| 0.0544, a margin of 0.0021. Both values are confirmed, but the margin is far below the Monte Carlo and sampling resolution.
(5) FINDINGS.md was last touched at d083547d and contains no vx results yet, so there are no written claims to check against.

minor_issues: IMPORTANT (design, not computation). The noise floor is a single replicate pair, and all 14 id rep1 runs ran as the last block of the batch. In runs_vx/_logs/sim.log they sit at positions 68-92 of 92, after every rep0 and every arm run. rep1 tipped later: in 5 of the 6 bases where both reps tipped, rep1 was later by 2-9 rounds (sign test p = 0.22). Mean tip round is 25.0 vs 20.8, and 6 of 7 rep1 tips came after the deadline vs 1 of 6 in rep0. So Δ_noise mixes seed noise with a possible run-order effect. 9 of 12 monitors have a negative Δ_noise, e.g. clock -0.196 [-0.292, -0.092] and oracle -0.115 [-0.193, -0.051]. Every shift is measured against rep0, which is the easier replicate for most monitors. None of the six lenses connected the late tipping to the run order.

IMPORTANT (H2 is a weak test). The time arm moved the deadline (17-26 to 29) but did not move tipping beyond replicate timing. Time-arm tips came at mean round 24.9 (range 19-31), the same as id rep1 (25.0). 5 of 8 fell in rounds 19-25, where the frozen clock scores highest: it peaks at 0.129 in round 18, the only round above its threshold of 0.1207, and is about 6e-6 from round 29 on. So M(time) - M(id rep1) compares two blocks with the same mean tip round, and a clock that does not collapse (+0.084 [-0.086, +0.267]) is what one would expect. Separately, the frozen clock alarms at round 18 in every untipped run whatever the deadline. That is a deployment mistiming the AUROC metric cannot see.

Manipulation checks. (1) enf did not reduce tipping: 5/14 vs 6/14 (K4 1/9 vs 3/9, K2 4/5 vs 3/5). (2) glm shifted the base rate (13/14 tipped; 88% of glm negative rows come from tipped runs vs 30% in id rep0) and message volume (1708 vs 1278 judged messages), but not the jury semantics: every KS D is <= 0.048, inside the replicate KS of 0.003-0.049. (3) topo is only a factor-level twin, on 7 bases. In three of the four arms the intended stress condition therefore did not clearly arise.

Realized resolution is about twice as coarse as planned. Median AUROC shift-CI half-width is 0.129 over 48 CIs (VALIDATION §3.5 planned 0.06-0.10). For gnn it is 0.16-0.22 on shift and 0.16-0.26 on shift minus noise; the time-matched median is 0.27. The percentile CIs are also anticonservative (about 2x nominal error in the pre-eval null simulations, worse for topo). The sentence in ANALYSIS_PLAN §6.6, 'erkennt nur Einbrüche > 0,1 AUROC. Das steht so im Paper', has to be corrected to roughly 0.15-0.25.

H4 'nicht gestützt' is correct under the pre-registered definition (vx_eval.py, frozen since 4e6e998; §6.4 plus Nachtrag 2 item 7), but it sits on a knife edge. The gnn alarmed in 3/9 untipped enf runs vs 1/8 id rep0 runs (Fisher p = 0.58). One fewer enf alarm, or one more id alarm, flips it. New in this audit: id rep0 K4-027 peaks at 0.3126, only 0.0014 below the gnn threshold of 0.3140. must_not_claim: 'The monitors are robust to time, population, enforcement and topology shifts.' The defensible claim is only 'no evidence of a drop larger than about 0.15-0.25 AUROC'.
'The suite detects drops > 0.1 AUROC' (the plan's §6.6 wording). The realized resolution is about 0.15-0.25.

'1 of 5 hypotheses confirmed', 'H5 shows the graph signal holds on hub networks', or 'the GNN is more robust to topology than bag'. H5 is a point rule on 7 bases, its CI includes 0, and it reverses on time-matched AUROC.

'H1 shows the GNN reads dynamics', or the reverse. The CI [0.45, 0.97] covers both readings. Also not: 'the GNN separates the id replicates perfectly (1.000)', which rests on a single pair with a degenerate CI.
'Part B is a blind within-config test' or 'LLM monitors are best within config on vx'. 10 of 29 pairs are night-night, and on the 19 pairs with a new run the LLMs drop to 0.68.

'The clock collapses under a longer sprint' or 'the time arm shows the GNN does not encode absolute time'. Tipping hardly moved in absolute time relative to the replicate, H2's GNN half passes by 0.002, and it fails on time-matched AUROC.
'GLM agents significantly increase tipping' (Holm p = 0.0625, and the counts were known before the plan) or 'visible enforcement reduces tipping' (5 vs 6 tipped).
'H3 shows generic semantics transfer to an unseen model' or 'the graph adds fragility'. The jury features barely shifted, and the difference -0.01 [-0.19, +0.20] is a coin flip.

'Enforcement makes the GNN raise false alarms' or 'an 8x false-alarm rate'. It is 3 vs 1 untipped runs (Fisher p = 0.58), all near misses. Nor the reverse: 'H4 holds' via the post-hoc paired-bases reading or a shifted threshold.
'Replicate noise is small' (FINDINGS §9). That is true only for outcome flips; in AUROC and tip timing it is large.

'Monitors improved under the shifts' (positive point shifts against the easy rep0), or 'zs:pairwise breaks under enforcement'. Its shift of -0.070 equals its own noise of -0.073; shift minus noise is +0.003 [-0.10, +0.13].

'The blind validation shows the LLM monitors beat the GNN', 'vx confirms the held-out ranking', or 'monitors beat the clock on vx'. No level test was pre-registered; on id rep0 the clock (0.823) is above the GNN (0.793); the +0.08 zs:global_full lead is exploratory and post hoc.
'The failed ordering shows the GNN is worse than simple baselines'. These are points without CIs, the ordering fails mainly on feat_pairwise > bag, and GNN >= bag+graph in every arm.
'vx shows a generalization gap or gain against held-out' (e.g. GNN 0.82 to 0.79, zs:global_full 0.82 to 0.91). The model instances, thresholds and population all differ.

Any 'CI excludes 0 (or 0.5)' statement for the seed-fragile intervals (glm zs:pairwise shift, the time zs tm shift-noise pair, glm oracle shift, H2-censored tm lower bound -0.0045, Part B zs:global_full 0.5157). 'The jury features shift under GLM' (e.g. success_claim). Every D is <= 0.048 and inside replicate noise, and a CI above 0 carries no evidence for a sup statistic.
